+The trainer calls reset(traj, k) to get the sandbox a branch starts from: the
+rollout `traj` (a replay-buffer record) as it was at step k. Returns the
+sandbox id; raises NotResettable when that state can't be restored.
+egress and fingerprints, never from knowing a particular env):
+1. Replay the prefix twice, in parallel, in fresh *scratch* tenants with the
+   sandbox clock shifted back to the rollout's own timeline, sending each
+   turn at its original `sent_at`. Both replays must reproduce every recorded
+   observation (modulo job-control PIDs, which fingerprint() also ignores)
+   and must agree exactly on fingerprint(), staging egress, admin-service
+   journals and shared-volume contents. Agreement of two independent replays
+   against the recorded screens is what licenses treating the replayed state
+   as the original state; any divergence (random values, sub-second
+   timestamps, mktemp names, ...) means the step cannot be restored.
+2. Produce the branch sandbox on the rollout's own tenant, with that tenant
+   put back to its state at step k:
+   - admin staging services are rewound / re-applied along their journal;
+   - shared volumes are restored from a tar captured at the right moment;
+   - a non-admin service cannot be rewound, so it must already sit at the
+     step-k state (no state-changing egress after k; checked by replaying
+     the suffix in the scratch tenant).
+   Production either replays the prefix once more on the restored tenant
+   (recreates shell / process / REPL state) or, when a files-only snapshot
+   provably reproduces the replay fingerprint, instantiates that snapshot.
+   The candidate is always verified against the replay fingerprint, the
+   admin journals and the volume hashes before it is returned.
+3. On any mismatch the tenant is rolled back where possible and
+   NotResettable is raised. Intermediate sandboxes/snapshots are always
+   disposed of, and a per-tenant file lock serialises concurrent workers
